summary.text: Michael DeCillis is the Democratic nominee in New York's 11th Congressional District. A Staten Island native, he has worked as a paramedic, New York City police officer, civil litigation attorney, legislative staffer in the State Assembly and special education teacher. He won the June 23 Democratic primary over Allison Ziogas; according to his campaign website, he is running to lower costs, protect Social Security and Medicare, strengthen public education and defend democratic institutions.

paragraphs.text: DeCillis describes himself as a fourth-generation Staten Islander and third-generation union member whose grandparents and parents were educators, city workers and union members; the Staten Island Advance reports that he now lives in Bay Ridge, and BK Reader says he has lived there for 14 years.

According to his campaign website, he volunteered as a teenager at the hospital where he was born, now Richmond University Medical Center, and became a volunteer EMT in college, and he graduated from Kalamazoo College.
He worked as a SWAT paramedic and field training officer in Michigan, where, per his campaign, he created the state's first K-9 unit pre-hospital emergency care program.
He was a first responder at Ground Zero on September 11, 2001, treating injured firefighters.
DeCillis then served about a decade as an NYPD officer and, while working full-time, earned a Juris Doctorate from New York Law School; he went on to work as a civil litigation attorney.

He later served as Chief of Staff and Director of Legislation for a member of the New York State Assembly, working on transparency measures and conditions for NYCHA residents, and as assistant counsel for the New York City Districting Commission; Ballotpedia and his campaign describe the Assembly job as a staff role, not an elected office.

He completed an AmeriCorps Teaching Fellowship and a Master's in Education at Hunter College, then taught special education in New York City District 75 schools, including students on the autism spectrum.
This is not DeCillis's first run for the seat: Ballotpedia lists him as a Democratic candidate who dropped out in March 2018 and as a withdrawn candidate in the 2022 Democratic primary.
In 2026 he won the June 23 Democratic primary.
